prompt: For an app with one payment provider, an engineer builds a plugin system in case they add more providers someday.
tells: in case they add more providers someday
why: Don't build for a future that may never come.
trap: There's only one case, so it isn't about duplication.

prompt: A simple report has 40 settings 'for flexibility'. No one has ever changed any of them.
tells: No one has ever changed any of them
why: Flexibility nobody uses is pure cost.
trap: Removing them may be cleanup, but the root error is building them.

prompt: In a system design interview for 1,000 users, a candidate adds sharding and multi-region failover 'for when we hit a billion'.
why: Design for the stated scale, and say how you'd grow.
trap: Scale is known (1,000 users); the problem is building past it.

prompt: A new service has one database table, but its author wrote a generic data layer that could support any database 'if we ever switch'.
why: Speculative generality adds cost now for an unlikely future.
trap: Not three cases of anything; it's one imagined future.

prompt: A reviewer asks the author to delete an unused extension hook: 'we can add it when a real caller shows up.'
tells: we can add it when a real caller shows up
why: Add it when it's needed, not before.
trap: The PR may get smaller, but the reason is not needing it.

prompt: Before launching to ten beta users, the team spends a month on an admin panel with role permissions for a support team they don't have.
tells: for a support team they don't have
why: Build for the users you have.
trap: No deadline pressure is described; it's speculative work.
